subject: Acceptance criteria, edge-case tests, and MAP timeline for evaluation
messages:
From: Evelyn Jansen <ejansen@acmehealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Eval acceptance criteria & timeline (Acme → Redwood)

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the routing failover you showed. Procurement and engineering want one tidy mutual action plan so we can move the trial forward without ambiguity. Specifically we need: a concise list of pass/fail acceptance tests, the exit gates (what causes us to stop the trial), and a timeline to production should the trial pass.

Can you send a MAP that:
- Defines 6–8 acceptance tests (functional + nonfunctional), with owners
- Calls out tolerances (e.g., 95th pct latency < 400ms under X QPS)
- Includes edge-case tests (HV/soft-failure, degraded models)
- Shows the handoff checklist for procurement for a POC->pilot conversion

We prefer the MAP by EOD Monday (18th) to present to the CTO on Tuesday. Also please include any artifacts we need to collect for SOC/evidence in parallel.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Jansen
Head of Platform Integrations — Acme Health
E: ejansen@acmehealth.com
P: +1 415-555-0182

Attachment: acme_trial_scope_v1.pdf (referenced)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Evelyn Jansen <ejansen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval acceptance criteria & timeline (Acme → Redwood)

Evelyn —

Appreciate the clear ask. Draft MAP attached (redwood_MAP_v0.2.pdf) and a short acceptance_test_matrix.xlsx with measured tolerances. High level summary below so you can share with the CTO quickly.

Summary (short):
- Scope: 2-week trial with seeded traffic (QA + production-like synthetic set).
- Success: 6 primary acceptance tests across functional, latency, cost, and safety with per-test owners. All tests must pass, or we agree a mitigated re-run cadence.
- Exit gates: (1) critical safety regression, (2) sustained tail latency above threshold for >10m, (3) >5% request failure rate for 30m, (4) inability to reach agreed SLA on quantization/throughput for 2 business days.
- Edge cases: degraded-model fallback (auto-route to smaller model), KV-cache warmup failure, upstream region outage. Each has a runbook and expected observable signal.
- Handoff: procurement milestone checklist included — SOC evidence bundle (log retention, audit trails, encryption certs), commercial terms to convert to Dedicated.

Owners and next steps:
- I will own MAP delivery and runbook alignment (Rishi).
- Marissa will lead acceptance test verification and demo artifacts (Marissa).
- Ben will confirm cost/run-rate estimation for trial (Ben).
- Jasmine will handle security evidence and coordinate with your compliance team (Jasmine).

Can you confirm the trial traffic window and whether Acme will provide a tokenized subset of live requests for fidelity testing? If you approve we’ll run the internal smoke verification tomorrow and share the final MAP + matrix by EOD.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0119

Attachments: redwood_MAP_v0.2.pdf, acceptance_test_matrix.xlsx
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Evelyn Jansen <ejansen@acmehealth.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval acceptance criteria & timeline (Acme → Redwood)

Thanks Rishi — quick note from the verification side.

I've sketched the acceptance tests in the matrix with pass criteria and a short verification protocol for each:
1) Functional correctness: 1k sample prompts, >= 92% accuracy on labeled set, owner: Marissa
2) Latency: 95th percentile < 380ms at 50 QPS sustained for 10m, owner: Marissa
3) Throughput: sustained 120 tokens/s per GPU under batching profile, owner: Ben (bench run attached)
4) Safety/False Positive flags: <= 0.5% on our safety metric across sample set, owner: Jasmine
5) Degraded model fallback: automatic routing validated by inducing 30% GPU failure during a 5m window; must complete with <2x latency penalty, owner: Ben
6) Persistence / KV warmup: restore time < 8s for 99% of sessions, owner: Marissa

Edge-case acceptance: For each edge-case we list observable signals and remediation steps (see matrix). If any edge-case test fails, remediation window is 48 hours and a single re-run is permitted before escalation.

Note on SOC evidence: Jasmine — I flagged the specific log extracts Acme will want (token-level latency histogram, audit trail for model version selection).

We also added a demo script and evidence checklist page in the MAP so Acme's CTO can see the artifacts quickly.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: acceptance_test_matrix.xlsx
From: Evelyn Jansen <ejansen@acmehealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, Daniel Park <dpark@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval acceptance criteria & timeline (Acme → Redwood)

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Short answers:
- Acme can provide a tokenized subset of live traffic for fidelity testing (will deliver by Thu 21st).
- CTO reviewed the summary and wants the trial to start Mon Jun 25, with a 2-week run and a mid-point check-in at day 7.
- Procurement: the SOC evidence items you listed are sufficient for initial review; legal will follow for commercial terms once the MAP completes.

Please proceed with the internal smoke tomorrow. Marissa — can you include the demo script as a 10‑minute compressed artifact for the CTO?

We’ll treat the attached MAP and matrix as the working agreement for the trial — procurement will keep a copy for the file.

Best,
Evelyn
